_schema_notes.coverage: Authoritative schema for all DID formats — DD Form 1664 (pre-2014) and free-text (post-2014 MIL-STD-963C)
_schema_notes.did_format: Set to 'dd_form_1664' or 'free_text'. Determines which fields are expected to be populated.
_schema_notes.963c_compliant: True if the DID was prepared under MIL-STD-963C (2014 or later). False for older DIDs.
_schema_notes.reserved_fields: Fields marked RESERVED are present in one format but not the other. Always include them — set to empty string or empty array when not applicable.
_schema_notes.preparation_instructions: Official MIL-STD-963C name for what was previously called 'requirements'. Contains the numbered sections of the DID. All section numbers are normalized to strictly numeric dot-notation (1, 1.1, 1.1.1). Letter-based source numbering (2.a, 3.1.b) is converted to numeric equivalents (2.1, 3.1.2).
_schema_notes.asterisk: True if the requirement number is followed by * in the source document (conditional requirement).

title: Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management (C-SCRM) Software Bill of Material (SBOM) Requirements
summary: Specifies requirements for a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) that includes comprehensive software component information and upstream relationship assertions, in alignment with CISA and NTIA guidelines, to support Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management (C-SCRM) activities.
use_relationship:
Data delivered using this Data Item Description (DID) specifies the requirements for a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) that includes comprehensive software component information and upstream relationship assertions in alignment with CISA and NTIA guidelines. The SBOM will ensure suppliers/vendors maintain and/or improve Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management (C-SCRM) activities. This approach provides a consistent and repeatable approach for sharing product component data.

a. SBOM Types. Vendors should specify the type of SBOM provided based on the software development stage. Possible types include Design, Source, Build, Analyzed, Deployed, and Runtime SBOMs.

b. Each software component entry must include information about its upstream relationships.

c. The word "item" is used throughout the document to refer to software components of the system.

d. This DID contains the format, content, and intended use information for the data product resulting from the work task described in the solicitation.

e. This DID should be tailored in the Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL) to include only the required specific data elements from Table 1. Examples of specific uses for the data and the data elements that could be used for each purpose follows:

(1) Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) data can be used to establish the details and supply chain relationships of various components used in building in a system. The SBOM will provide managers essential information that enables the identification, forecasting, mitigation, and management of software security. The data will be used to form a foundational data layer on which further security tools, practices, and assurances can be built.

preparation_instructions.title: Format
preparation_instructions.content: The C-SCRM SBOM shall be submitted in English and machine-readable format to ensure interoperability and automation support.

preparation_instructions.title: Content
preparation_instructions.content: Include a complete inventory of all first party and third party components in the SBOM. The data shall contain the information specified by the contract as referenced by the Data Items in Table 1. The data shall meet the requirements as specified in the Description column of Table 1. All fields designated by the contract shall be included. Fields for which data is not available shall be left blank. The data shall be included to the lowest indenture level (component level) for all items, including subcontractor items. Adhere to NTIA guidance on documenting upstream relationships, ensuring transparency and clarity in the software supply chain as referenced in Example 1.

children.title: Vulnerability-Exploitability eXchange (VEX) Information
children.content: In addition to SBOM data, vendors are encouraged to provide VEX information for each software component listed in the SBOM, where such information is available and applicable.

children.title: The VEX should include, for each vulnerability
children.content: The VEX should include, for each vulnerability, a status (e.g., Not affected, Affected, Fixed, Under Investigation) and any recommended actions or remediation to address the vulnerability.

children.title: VEX information should be regularly updated
children.content: VEX information should be regularly updated to reflect the status of vulnerabilities, especially after significant software updates or when new vulnerabilities are discovered.

children.title: Vendors should ensure that VEX data
children.content: Vendors should ensure that VEX data is synchronized with the corresponding SBOM data.
